results.title: Photonic and Phononic Properties of Engineered ...
results.content: The outstanding potentials of such meta-devices to revolutionalize communications, sensing, information, and energy technologies along with the existence of several challenges in design, optimization, fabrication, and characterization of such structures have inspired extensive research activities in the field of engineered nanostructure materials and devices. Highly nonlinear materials and photonic nanostructures are essential components for resonant optoelectronic devices with enhanced bandwidth and sensitivity, such as nonlinear optical biosensors, photodetectors, and ultrafast optical switches. In particular, I will present the design, fabrication, and nonlinear optical characterization of strongly-coupled nano-antennas with multiple BICs for enhanced photon detection on the Si platform. In this talk I will present our recent progress in developing such a modeling framework and applying it to reconfigurable photonic devices, with examples spanning phase-change materials based tunable metamaterials and integrated optics components. We propose an all-optical nonlinear activation function for deep optical neural networks by modulating the refractive index of a high-Q dielectric metasurface via non-degenerate two-photon absorption of co-propagating signal and pump beams.

results.title: Course Schedule - Trinity College
results.content: In this course, students will discover Trinity's and Hartford's place in slavery's vast social, cultural, economic, and political networks. |  | This course guides and supports American Studies majors, as well as interested students in other interdisciplinary programs, as they complete original research and writing for their capstone project (this can be a 1 or 2 semester project). Through texts, seminar discussions, films, and a field-based research project as the major exercise, students will explore a number of issues, including cultural persistence and the loss of place; the meaning of the frontier and indigenous land rights struggles; gender and public space; the deterritorialization of culture (i.e., McDonald’s in Hong Kong); and the cultural costs of an increasingly "fast" and high-tech world.
